questions.question: With ggplot2 loaded and `d <- tibble(t = 1:4, a = c(3, 5, 4, 6), b = c(1, 2, 2, 3))`, what does `ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x = t, y = a), color = "red3") + geom_point(aes(x = t, y = b))` draw?
options: Eight red points, as a colour set in one layer applies to the whole plot.
Eight black points, as a colour written outside `aes()` is ignored.
An error, because `color` may only be given inside `aes()`.
Four red points for `a` and four black points for `b`.

questions.question: In `ggplot(d, aes(x = Year, y = Sales)) + geom_point()`, the geom is replaced by `geom_line()` and nothing else changes. What changes in the plot?
options: The axes: `geom_line()` puts `Year` on the y-axis and `Sales` on the x-axis.
Only the marks: a line instead of points, with the same mapping.
The data: `geom_line()` first sums `Sales` over the years before drawing.
Nothing, because the mapping in `aes()` decides the type of plot.

questions.question: A student runs `p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = t, y = a)) + geom_point()`, where `d` is a tibble with numeric columns `t` and `a`. No plot appears. Why?
options: It was stored in `p`; typing `p` prints the object and draws it.
The call failed without a message, because `ggplot()` needs a `data =` argument.
ggplot2 draws a plot only after `show()` has been added as a final layer.
Assigning a plot deletes it, so the code must be run again without `p <-`.

questions.question: A tibble has numeric columns `income`, `spending` and `household` (number of people). What does `size = household` do in `geom_point(aes(x = income, y = spending, size = household))`?
options: It sets every point to one fixed size, given by the text `household`.
It sorts the points by `household` before they are drawn.
It draws larger households as larger points, with a size legend.
It gives an error, because `size` must be a number such as `size = 3`.

questions.question: With ggplot2 loaded and `d <- tibble(t = 1:4, a = c(3, 5, 4, 6), b = c(1, 2, 2, 3))`, what does `p <- ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x = t, y = a)) + geom_line(aes(x = t, y = a)) + labs(title = "T"); length(p[["layers"]])` return?
With ggplot2 loaded and `d <- tibble(t = 1:4, a = c(3, 5, 4, 6), b = c(1, 2, 2, 3))`, what does `ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x = t, y = a, color = "darkgreen"))` draw?
options: Salmon red points and a legend with the single entry `darkgreen`.
Dark green points and no legend, as the colour is a fixed setting.
Dark green points and a legend with the single entry `darkgreen`.
An error, because `d` has no column called `darkgreen`.

questions.question: A student types `p <- ggplot(d)` on one line and `+ geom_point(aes(x = t, y = a))` on the next line, and runs both. What happens?
options: A scatter plot is stored in `p`, as R joins a line that starts with `+` to the previous one.
An error, and `p` does not exist afterwards because the whole command failed.
A scatter plot is stored in `p`, with a warning that `+` should end the first line.
The second line gives an error, and `p` holds an empty plot without any layer.

questions.question: With dplyr and ggplot2 loaded and `d` a tibble with numeric columns `t` and `a`, what happens when R runs `ggplot(d, aes(x = t, y = a)) %>% geom_point()`?
options: A scatter plot of `a` against `t`, since `%>%` and `+` do the same job.
An error, as the pipe passes the plot to `geom_point()` as its mapping.
An empty plot without points, since the pipe drops the layer silently.
A scatter plot, with a warning to use `+` instead of `%>%` next time.

questions.question: For a stored scatter plot `p`, which line sets the y-axis label to `Emissions` and the title to `CO2` in one call?
options: `p + labs(y = "Emissions", title = "CO2")`
`p + labs("Emissions", "CO2")`
`p + ylab("Emissions", "CO2")`
`p + aes(y = "Emissions", title = "CO2")`

questions.question: A tibble `d` has numeric `t` and `a` and a column `sector` with the values `"retail"`, `"energy"`, `"retail"`, `"farming"`. What legend does `ggplot(d, aes(x = t, y = a, color = sector)) + geom_point()` draw?
options: A legend titled `sector` with four entries, one per row of `d`.
A legend titled `colour` with entries retail, energy, farming.
No legend, as ggplot2 picks the colours automatically.
A legend titled `sector` with entries energy, farming, retail.

questions.question: A plot has two point layers, one with `color = "black"` and one with `color = "red3"` written outside `aes()`. Why does it have no legend, and how is one obtained?
options: Legends need at least three colours; adding a third coloured layer makes one appear.
A legend appears only after `labs(color = "Sector")` has given it a title.
They are settings; map `color` to a sector column of long data instead.
Legends are made only for mappings in `ggplot()`; move both colours into `ggplot()`.

questions.question: For a tibble `d` with numeric columns `t` and `a`, what does `ggplot(d, aes(x = t, y = a))` draw on its own, without any geom?
options: A scatter plot, because points are the default geom of `ggplot()`.
An empty panel with axes for `t` and `a`, but no points or lines.
An error, because a plot needs at least one layer before printing.
A line through the rows, because the mapping has both x and y.

questions.question: Emissions of five sectors over ten years are stored either wide (one column per sector) or long (columns `Year`, `Sector`, `Emissions`). Why is the long form easier to plot with ggplot2?
options: One mapping `color = Sector` colours all sectors and adds a legend.
Long data need no `aes()` at all, because ggplot2 detects the columns itself.
Long data have fewer rows, so ggplot2 draws them faster than wide data.
Wide data cannot be plotted with ggplot2, since only long data have numeric columns.

questions.question: With ggplot2 loaded and `d <- tibble(t = 1:4, a = c(3, 5, 4, 6), b = c(1, 2, 2, 3))`, how is the y-axis of `ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x = t, y = a)) + geom_point(aes(x = t, y = b))` labelled?
options: `b`, the column of the last layer added
`y`, as the layers map different columns
It has no label, as the layers disagree
`a`, the column of the first mapping

questions.question: With ggplot2 loaded and `d <- tibble(t = 1:4, a = c(3, 5, 4, 6), b = c(1, 2, 2, 3))`, what does `p1 <- ggplot(d, aes(x = t, y = a)) + geom_point(); p2 <- p1 + geom_line(); length(p1[["layers"]])` return?
With dplyr and ggplot2 loaded and `d <- tibble(t = 1:4, a = c(3, 5, 4, 6))`, which line draws the rows with `a > 3` as points?
options: `d %>% filter(a > 3) %>% ggplot(d, aes(x = t, y = a)) + geom_point()`
`d %>% filter(a > 3) + ggplot(aes(x = t, y = a)) + geom_point()`
`d %>% filter(a > 3) %>% ggplot(aes(x = t, y = a)) + geom_point()`
`ggplot(aes(x = t, y = a)) + geom_point(d %>% filter(a > 3))`

questions.question: A tibble has `Year`, numeric `v` and `Country` (two countries, three years each). What does `ggplot(d, aes(x = Year, y = v)) + geom_point(aes(color = Country)) + geom_line()` draw?
options: Points coloured by country and one black zigzag line through all six points.
Points and lines both coloured by country: two lines, with a shared legend.
Points coloured by country and no line, since `geom_line()` lacks a colour.
Black points and one line, since mappings must sit in `ggplot()` to take effect.

questions.question: A scatter plot shows `Transport` against `Year` for three countries over five years, one point per country and year. Why is it not the graph of a function of `Year`?
options: Because a graph needs a formula, and the points come from data.
Because the points are not connected; adding `geom_line()` makes it a graph.
Because `Year` takes whole numbers only, while a graph needs real inputs.
Because each year has three points; a function gives one value per input.

questions.question: With ggplot2 loaded and `d <- tibble(t = 1:4, a = c(3, 5, 4, 6), b = c(1, 2, 2, 3))`, what does `ggplot(d, aes(x = t, y = a)) + geom_point() + geom_point(aes(y = b), color = "red3")` draw?
options: Four red points for `b` only, as the second `geom_point()` replaces the first.
Four red points for `a` only, as the mapping in `ggplot()` overrides `y = b`.
Four black points for `a` and four red points for `b`, at the same x positions.
An error, because `aes(y = b)` replaces the inherited mapping and leaves no x.

questions.question: With dplyr and ggplot2 loaded, what does `d <- tibble(t = 1:4, a = c(3, 5, 4, 6)); p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = t, y = a)) + geom_point(); d <- filter(d, a > 4); nrow(layer_data(p))` return?
